# What Docker personal access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is twenty-seven base64url characters, so the run and
# eleven more of it are one, and the nine character prefix in front brings a
# token to thirty-six. Two cases carry the alphabet's other letters and are
# built from ordered runs of their own instead: the twenty-six letters of the
# upper case ascending, and the twenty-six of the lower case descending, each
# with a trailing digit to reach the count.

patterns: docker-personal-access-token

# The prefix Docker writes a personal access token with, in the places a token
# is written: the environment a build reads it from, the command it logs in
# with, and the request that exchanges it for a bearer token.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=«docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the command a user logs in with
in:       docker login -u myusername -p dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      docker login -u myusername -p «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the body a request exchanges it in
in:       {"identifier":"myusername","secret":"dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}
out:      {"identifier":"myusername","secret":"«docker-personal-access-token»"}

case:     a token in the file a workflow writes it into
in:       registry-password: dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      registry-password: «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in a docker config.json
in:       {"auths":{"registry.example.com":{"auth":"dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a"}}}
out:      {"auths":{"registry.example.com":{"auth":"«docker-personal-access-token»"}}}

case:     a token between tabs
in:       field\tdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a\tnext
out:      field\t«docker-personal-access-token»\tnext

case:     a token followed by crlf
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a\r\n
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=«docker-personal-access-token»\r\n

# The alphabet the twenty-seven characters are written in: base64url, which is
# the letters of both cases, the digits, the hyphen and the underscore. What it
# leaves out is the two characters standard base64 writes in place of the last
# of those, so a payload carrying either is no body. The prefix is read in
# lowercase alone, since the uppercase spelling is the shape an environment
# variable's name is written in.

case:     a body carrying a hyphen and an underscore
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789_
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a plus in the body
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef+123456789a

case:     a slash in the body
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef/123456789a

case:     a body of uppercase letters
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQ
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a body carrying the lowercase letters past the run
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopq
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       DCKR_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DCKR_PAT_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     hyphens where the prefix carries its underscores
in:       dckr-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr-pat-0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     the kind with one letter capitalized
in:       dckr_Pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr_Pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

# The lengths either side of twenty-seven. Docker states no length, so the count
# is read off the published tokens and the rulesets that agree on them, and it
# is used as a count rather than a floor: twenty-six characters are not a token,
# and twenty-eight are a token and one character that belongs to no credential.
# The second of those is the price of having no boundary behind the match — a
# boundary there would drop this token rather than trim it, and a real token
# written against a character of the alphabet would come through whole.

case:     a body of twenty-seven characters is a token
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a body of twenty-six characters is not
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789ab
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»b

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN_dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN_«docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      x«docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a token before a hyphenated word
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a-suffix
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»-suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a.
out:      the token is «docker-personal-access-token».

case:     a token between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       日本語dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a日本語
out:      日本語«docker-personal-access-token»日本語

# Two tokens written together. Every character of the prefix belongs to the
# alphabet a body is written in, so a token can begin anywhere inside the one
# before it: the prefix written twice with a body behind the second is a token
# from either prefix, the two spans overlap and the whole of it is redacted as
# one. Written without that overlap the two are separate values and both go.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789adckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»«docker-personal-access-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       dckr_pat_dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      «docker-personal-access-token»

case:     two different tokens on one line separated by a space
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef-123456789_
out:      «docker-personal-access-token» «docker-personal-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix is nine characters of
# an alphabet of sixty-four, so a base64url payload long enough to spell it
# carries a candidate, and the twenty-seven behind it are in the alphabet by
# construction. That is the answer rather than a fault in it, because sparing it
# would spare a real token: the vendor's format is that prefix and that many of
# those characters, and no part of it is left for such a run to fail. Standard
# base64 and hexadecimal write no underscore at all, so neither carries a
# candidate at however long it runs.

case:     the prefix inside a longer base64url run
in:       payload=zzzzdckr_pat_0123456789abcdef0123456789azzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«docker-personal-access-token»zzzz

case:     a standard base64 payload, which carries no underscore
in:       payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdckrpat0123456789abcdef
out:      payload=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEAdckrpat0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first two are the second prefix
# Docker's credential table names, the organization access token's, written to
# each of the two widths that have been claimed for it: the width Docker's own
# API reference prints and the width the rulesets reading that format ask for.
# Then a body a space has broken, and two inputs carrying no prefix at all: a
# run of the right length opening with something else, and a line of prose,
# which holds nothing as long as a body and no run unbroken by a space.

case:     an organization access token at the width the reference prints
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     an organization access token at the width the rulesets ask for
in:       dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dckr_oat_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body broken by a space
in:       dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a
out:      dckr_pat_0123456789abcdef 123456789a

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789a
out:      xxxx_xxx_0123456789abcdef0123456789a

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And the shape Docker Hub's login endpoint took before a prefix was written in
# front of one, which the pattern's own file weighs: a UUID carrying nothing to
# be recognised by but the vendor's word beside it. Such a token reaching a log
# stays in the output whole, because a pattern reading it would redact every
# UUID a caller passes through.

case:     the shape a token took before a prefix was written in front of one
in:       DOCKER_TOKEN=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      DOCKER_TOKEN=01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a log line naming the registry a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="pushing an image" url=https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/nginx/tags
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="pushing an image" url=https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/nginx/tags
